--- title: "[StepFilter]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-class}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Remove rows that do not match a predicate. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/tidymodels/shoez/blob/examples-section/shoez/step_filter.py#L69-L206){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.CLASS} ```python StepFilter(predicate, id=None) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Rows for which ``predicate`` is not ``True`` are dropped. Filtering applies to the training data only. Fitting a recipe drops the non-matching training rows, but transforming new data returns every row given to it, because dropping rows from data being scored would silently lose predictions. So a recipe that filters is not a way to filter new data. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [predicate]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Predicate]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Callable taking the frame and returning a boolean narwhals expression or series, ``True`` for the rows to keep. Must be callable. [id]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Stable step identifier. Default ``"filter"``. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Rows where ``age`` is 30 or below are dropped when the recipe is fitted, while ``transform()`` leaves every row in place: ::: {#8ed097ff .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} df = pd.DataFrame({"age": [25, 41, 33, 52]}) df ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
age
0 25
1 41
2 33
3 52
``` ::: ::: Specifying the step touches no data: ::: {#7056e9e9 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} recipe = Recipe().add(StepFilter(lambda df: df["age"] > 30)) recipe ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` Recipe (untrained) Inputs: no roles assigned Steps: step_filter() [untrained] ``` ::: ::: `fit()` applies the predicate to the training data: ::: {#d7549ccd .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} fitted = recipe.fit(df) fitted ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` Recipe (trained) Inputs: 1 columns — 1 predictor Steps: step_filter(age) [trained] ``` ::: ::: `transform()` leaves new data untouched, so all four rows come back: ::: {#c9d445e3 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} fitted.transform(df) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ```{=html}
age
0 25
1 41
2 33
3 52
``` ::: :::
